title: Cell-Tower, Digital-Billboard & IOS Lease Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Pricing Cell Site Buyouts, Policing Lease Fine Print, Negotiating Ground Rent, and Underwriting Tower and Billboard Permits Before Any Money Changes Hands

worksheets.title: Cell Site Buyout Valuation and Fine-Print Audit
worksheets.purpose: Price a cell site rent stream the way buyers do, then audit the lease language that moves the multiple, so every buyout offer is measured against documented multiples, named sub-tenants, termination risk, and fine print before any letter of intent is signed.
instructions: Gather the full lease, every amendment, twelve months of rent statements, and every buyout offer letter before filling in a single field.
Physically verify sub-tenants on site through meter labels, equipment cabinets, and building department permits rather than relying on pay stubs.
Run every dollar figure at three multiples, aggregator low, average, and clean-lease high, and keep the math visible on the page.
Do not sign or return any letter of intent until the right of first refusal, confidentiality, and consent-to-assign review is finished.
Demand written letters of intent and sample easement documents from every buyer, and log each one against its likely money source.

fields.name: current_annual_rent_and_multiple
fields.prompt: Record the exact annual cell site rent your lease pays today, then multiply it by the low, average, and clean-lease multiples practitioners quote. Show all three dollar results side by side so you know the realistic ceiling and floor before any buyer calls.
fields.example: Annual rent is $18,000. At 17.5 times that equals $315,000, the figure Casella attaches to a lease carrying a right of first refusal or other limiting language [Tower Genius — pSGbaA0AbTo @ 00:02:07]. At 19 times with 3% escalators, revenue share, and no ROFR, the same stream reaches $342,000. Aggregator offers at 8 to 15 times would land between $144,000 and $270,000.

fields.name: discount_rate_present_value
fields.prompt: Write down the discount rate each buyer is implicitly using and compare it with an owner-side rate. Estimate the present value of your remaining term with escalators, then state the gap in dollars between that value and the highest written offer.
fields.example: Aggregators discount at 8 to 12 percent while owner-side valuations run 4 to 6 percent. At 8 percent, an $18,000-a-year lease with a 3% escalator and 25 years of term is worth about $250,000, or 14 times rent [Acquisition Insider — MtWLazzJb9Y @ 00:02:26]. My written high offer is $230,000, so the documented gap is roughly $20,000 before any owner-rate adjustment.

fields.name: subtenant_identification
fields.prompt: List every carrier physically on the tower or rooftop by name, not as collocator A, B, or C. Note how you confirmed each one, such as meter labels, cabinets, or permits, and flag any tenant buyers treat as risky.
fields.example: Pay stubs list only collocator A, B, and C, which buyers reject because they want to rule out carriers like Dish before wiring money [Tower Genius — X75LHgvP1U8 @ 00:01:36]. Meter labels show AT&T and T-Mobile; a cabinet sticker and a building department permit confirm the third occupant is Dish. Flag: toxic exposure, expect a discounted bid or walkaway.

fields.name: rofr_confidentiality_consent
fields.prompt: Quote the exact right of first refusal, confidentiality, and consent-to-assign clauses from your lease. For each, explain how it could suppress bidding or put you in default if you signed a letter of intent without clearing it first.
fields.example: Section 14 grants the tenant a right of first refusal. One Tower Genius client shopping a ROFR-encumbered lease to about six top easement buyers drew only three bids [Tower Genius — 5MqJqF4hVEQ @ 00:01:28]. Section 22 confidentiality bars disclosing rent, so signing a letter of intent before clearing it could trigger default and kill the sale [Tower Genius — wpxdOZZukBY @ 00:05:12].

fields.name: rofr_price_penalty
fields.prompt: Estimate the dollar penalty a right of first refusal imposes on your specific buyout by comparing a clean-lease multiple against your encumbered multiple. Record both totals and the difference so the cost of leaving the clause in place is explicit.
fields.example: Casella's three-carrier urban rooftop paid $117,000 a year; at 19 times the buyout reached $2,223,000, and ROFRs would have cut about $200,000, pushing it under $2 million [Tower Genius — pSGbaA0AbTo @ 00:07:14]. Separately, a retiring owner who struck the ROFR was offered over $200,000 above their best offer [Tower Genius — H0Q5FZ_5RWA @ 00:04:14]. Both figures set my strike-the-clause priority.

fields.name: money_source_map
fields.prompt: Map every buyout company that has contacted you to the money source behind it, as far as you can determine. Note duplicate offers that may trace to one funder and record which buyers supplied written letters of intent and sample easement documents.
fields.example: Four mailers arrived from different buyout companies, yet a handful of money sources sit behind roughly 20 brands, so four offers may share one funder [Tower Genius — P2LhXcxO5KE @ 00:01:07]. I demanded written letters of intent and sample easements; five buyers narrowed to two, and a four-month clawback surfaced only on paper [James Furlo | Furlo Capital — bk4EnTlbPdA @ 00:18:34].

fields.name: sell_or_hold_timing
fields.prompt: Decide whether to sell the rent stream now and transfer obsolescence risk, or hold and renegotiate at renewal. Record years remaining until renewal, any offer arriving on the eve of renewal, and the reasoning that tips your decision either way.
fields.example: Renewal is 26 months away and an unsolicited offer just landed. Buyers love an undervalued lease on the eve of renewal because the wider spread is their arbitrage play [Tower Genius — wpxdOZZukBY @ 00:03:34]. Decision: hold, renegotiate escalator and revenue share first, then shop the improved stream. Once sold, no other income remains from that site [Tower Genius — weiPEHNdlU0 @ 00:02:07].

fields.name: termination_stress_test
fields.prompt: Model the rent stopping entirely in year five through eight and describe what happens to your income and your buyout value. Reference the Dish rent halt, then decide whether one site can survive that scenario or whether diversification is required.
fields.example: Dish halted rent on about 25,000 sites, and buyers price that termination risk into every bid. Acquisition Insider's rule: model rent stopping in year five to eight, and if one site cannot survive it, buy several or pass [Acquisition Insider — MtWLazzJb9Y @ 00:06:38]. My single-tenant rooftop fails the test, which argues for selling now rather than holding.

fields.name: rooftop_premises_definition
fields.prompt: Check whether your rooftop or ground lease defines the premises with written dimensions. Record the documented square footage, the equipment actually installed, and every antenna or remote radio unit that should be billed as an expansion under a tightened definition.
fields.example: A West Coast T-Mobile rooftop amendment had no premises dimensions written anywhere after roughly 20 years on the roof [Tower Genius — WlOtjvRO-jU @ 00:01:23]. My lease likewise omits dimensions. Proposed fix: define a 400-square-foot area plus two wall mounts in writing, so any added antenna or wall-mounted RRU becomes a billable expansion, and keep the renewal term short.

fields.name: optimization_letter_response
fields.prompt: Draft your response to any lease optimization or rent reduction letter you have received. Name the carrier involved, state the question you will ask about equipment removal, and note who you will copy so the bluff is called in writing.
fields.example: A tower company letter demands a $500 monthly rent cut. Reply: 'Please confirm when the equipment will be removed,' copying the carrier named on the letter [Tower Genius — Z2FKmFdZgvA @ 00:10:10]. An area director once called within 48 hours begging that it not be treated as termination. Sites usually move only under eminent domain, not over $500 [Tower Genius — RMRSHif8WD0 @ 00:07:09].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when every carrier on site is named and physically verified, all three multiples are calculated in dollars, the right of first refusal, confidentiality, and consent clauses are quoted verbatim, the year-five-to-eight rent stop is modeled, and at least two written offers with sample easement documents are on file.

worksheets.title: Lease Negotiation and Ground Rent Capture
worksheets.purpose: Negotiate a cell site lease from the owner's side of the table by refusing to name a number first, compounding escalators, limiting space and use, and structuring revenue share as a percentage, then test whether nearby vacant land can produce truck parking or outdoor storage income.
instructions: Treat the carrier and the tower developer as the opposing side, and keep every exchange in writing from the first call forward.
Never sign a term sheet or option until you hold the full lease and know every term binding the whole property.
Keep co-location, sub-leasing, and revenue share out of early calls until the developer has done a site walk and spent money on engineering.
Value the individual site on its own merits and reject any argument built on so-called market rent or neighboring deals.
For any land screened for truck parking or outdoor storage, confirm surface, zoning, and highway access before projecting a single dollar.

fields.name: lessee_identity
fields.prompt: Identify whether the lessee is a carrier holding the site directly or a tower developer acting as middleman. Record the lessee's legal name and the realistic monthly rent range that identity implies before you respond to any number they propose.
fields.example: The lessee is a tower developer, not a carrier. Casella says a carrier-owned site supports about $2,000 a month while a developer realistically offers $750 to $1,000, because the developer spends $200,000 to $250,000 per tower and collects about $2,000 monthly per carrier tenant [Tower Genius — nUDRfQeqe7A @ 00:05:56]. Expect squeezed ground rent and negotiate structure, not just price.

fields.name: first_number_refusal
fields.prompt: Record every document the developer or carrier has sent, including term sheets and blank lease templates. Write the exact reply you will send that refuses to name a number first and demands proposed rent, term length, and escalation in writing.
fields.example: Received: one blank lease template and one term sheet. Tower Genius holds it is never a good idea to sign a term sheet [Tower Genius — Eo568DFPXFk @ 00:01:06]. Reply drafted: 'Thank you; please return this with your proposed rent, term length, and escalation filled in,' bouncing the template politely so I never negotiate against myself [Tower Genius — DJfkRMlj2fg @ 00:00:59].

fields.name: escalator_terms
fields.prompt: Write the escalator currently offered and the escalator you will demand. Compare a compounding annual increase against any five-year bump or CPI alternative, and calculate what each produces on your base rent at year ten and year twenty.
fields.example: The tower company offered 1 percent. Odum reports companies pushing 2, 1, or zero percent and insists on at least 3 percent compounding annually or CPI, noting 10 or 15 percent every five years does not compound each year [Vertical Consultants — F1m9euwLJAQ @ 00:04:23]. On $2,000 monthly base, 3 percent compounding reaches about $2,690 by year eleven.

fields.name: space_and_use_limits
fields.prompt: Record the square footage the developer requested versus what a tower actually needs, and list the permitted uses written into the draft. Treat time, space, and use as separate commodities and note what you will trade or withhold on each.
fields.example: The draft asks for 10,000 square feet. Odum says tower companies request up to 10,000 or more but need closer to 2,000 or 3,000 [Vertical Consultants — NS76BzQHI_o @ 00:01:00]. Counter: 2,500 square feet, use limited to wireless communications, any expansion priced separately. Time: initial term shortened so future renegotiation remains available rather than locked away for decades.

fields.name: revenue_share_structure
fields.prompt: Describe how revenue share is currently offered and restructure it as a percentage of what the tower owner collects from each collocator. Note when you will raise the subject so you do not reveal it before the developer commits money to the site.
fields.example: Their fallback is a flat $200 a month revenue share, a tactic Odum calls a fallback to give you something [Vertical Consultants — F1m9euwLJAQ @ 00:16:40]. Flat $400 against AT&T paying $2,000 is 20 percent, but only 10 percent once AT&T pays $4,000 [Vertical Consultants — eJhWsOIzk6A @ 00:01:05]. Counter: percentage share, raised only after their engineering spend.

fields.name: site_reconciliation
fields.prompt: Walk the site and reconcile the existing lease against what is physically installed. List any space used outside the lease lines, work done without consent, and unpaid taxes, insurance, utilities, or fees that create a renegotiation opening for you.
fields.example: The compound fence sits eight feet past the lease line, and a generator pad was added with no consent on file, the kind of painting outside the lines that hands owners an opening [Vertical Consultants — F1m9euwLJAQ @ 00:12:42]. Lease scan also shows property tax reimbursements unpaid for three years, a fee category that sometimes goes unpaid [Vertical Consultants — USOklBMqTr0 @ 00:00:55].

fields.name: expiration_leverage
fields.prompt: Record the years remaining before final expiration and place yourself on the leverage scale practitioners describe. Note any competing tower nearby, its mount height and elevation, and whether you plan to pause talks rather than be worn down.
fields.example: Seven years remain, which JP Tower Consulting calls significant leverage; within two years is stronger, and talks run 3 to 12 months or longer [JP Tower Consulting — gy9A1QN_8Jk @ 00:03:14]. A competing tower sits a mile east with lower mounts, which can force their hand. Tower Genius warns against letting the lease fall below two years, so talks start now.

fields.name: developer_commitment_check
fields.prompt: Before signing any option, ask the developer to name a committed carrier and a construction start date. Record their answers, how quickly they came, and whether they are asking for a right of first refusal they have not paid for.
fields.example: Asked for the committed carrier and start date; the developer answered 'pending' after two weeks, so they are treated as speculators whose option encumbers the property from day one [Vertical Consultants — 7qwoLJg7Ya8 @ 00:03:33]. The draft's ROFR gets struck: under the Gazella rule, a carrier wanting an option pays for it, like any Wall Street option [Tower Genius — xv8TdIdnmRQ @ 00:06:27].

fields.name: dollar_value_of_monthly_rent
fields.prompt: Translate every proposed monthly rent difference into lifetime lease value using the rule of thumb that one dollar of monthly rent equals roughly one thousand dollars of value. Record the gap between their offer and your counter in those terms.
fields.example: Their offer is $1,200 a month; my counter is $1,800. Odum's rule over a roughly 30-year lease life says each $1 of monthly rent is worth about $1,000, so an extra $100 a month is about $100,000 [Vertical Consultants — F1m9euwLJAQ @ 00:19:51]. The $600 gap therefore represents roughly $600,000 of lease value, which explains their resistance.

fields.name: vacant_land_income_screen
fields.prompt: If you hold vacant or underused land, assess it for truck parking or outdoor storage income. Record surface type, adjacency to retail or residential, highway access, zoning, and the daily or monthly rate band that matches your market density.
fields.example: Two acres of compacted gravel off an interstate in a suburban market, no retail or residential neighbors, passing Shealy's surface rule [Ask Flip Man — NIYpBpIvXTc @ 00:07:16]. Suburban rate band: $20 to $25 per truck per day. For a monthly model, Cauble pegs $175 to $225 per truck space, checked against local comps [Tyler Cauble — IRDT0HnPpUc @ 00:14:46].

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the lessee type is identified, a written counter specifying rent, term, a compounding escalator of at least 3 percent, square footage, permitted use, and percentage revenue share has been sent, the site reconciliation is logged, and no term sheet or option has been signed.

worksheets.title: Tower Ownership Returns and Billboard Permit Underwriting
worksheets.purpose: Underwrite a tower purchase or build on signed tenants, payback, and land control, then underwrite a billboard acquisition on permit status, ground lease, real occupancy, DOT traffic, and reroute risk, so both assets are priced as permit-protected infrastructure rather than steel.
instructions: Count only signed tenants; treat verbal prospects and hoped-for third tenants as zero when calculating returns and payback.
Line up the remaining ground lease term against payback for every structure before any purchase price is discussed.
Classify every billboard permit as conforming or nonconforming and confirm your state's re-erection rules in writing.
Source traffic counts and construction plans directly from the state DOT, never from the seller's package.
Build cash flow on twelve months of real occupancy and advertiser contracts, then apply a multiple only after every risk adjustment.

fields.name: tenant_count_returns
fields.prompt: Ask how many tenants are on the tower before anything else. Record the signed tenant count and the return band that count implies, and state plainly whether the structure clears the two-tenant line or remains a single-tenant gamble.
fields.example: One signed anchor only. Mr. Money puts returns near 6.5 percent with one tenant, about 13 percent with two, and approaching 20 percent with three [Mr. Money — jQ79QHMZWQE @ 00:07:36]. Economic Oddities calls a single-tenant tower a coin flip with a lease and draws the line at two tenants [Economic Oddities — QdFbgvbJJ-M @ 00:08:28]. Verdict: not yet underwritable.

fields.name: build_cost_payback
fields.prompt: Enter the modeled build cost, anchor rent, and margin for the tower, then calculate annual profit and payback years. Repeat the calculation with a second tenant added, including the extra capital required, so the jump in return is documented.
fields.example: On a $275,000 monopole, one tenant yields about $8,000 profit and a 34-year payback. A second tenant adds $30,000 revenue for $50,000 capex, lifting profit to $37,000 a year with under a 9-year payback, and about 97 percent of that revenue converts to profit [Mr. Finance — ku_-0C-ZnV4 @ 00:04:19]. My site matches this shape almost exactly.

fields.name: anchor_loss_stress
fields.prompt: Stress-test the loss of your anchor tenant and a carrier default. Record the revenue and profit decline, how long rent could stop, and what recovery you could realistically expect if a carrier stops paying across many sites at once.
fields.example: An anchor exit cuts revenue about 60 percent and profit about 78 percent [Mr. Finance — ku_-0C-ZnV4 @ 00:12:46]. Crown's Dish claim exceeds $3.5 billion with recovery uncertain [Profit Chain — t9bXdQI0jPM @ 00:08:38]. My tower's second tenant is Dish, so the stress case assumes zero Dish rent from year three and no recovery from any claim.

fields.name: land_control_match
fields.prompt: Compare the remaining ground lease term under the tower with the payback period you calculated. Record the gap, the renewal options, and whether you hold enough land control to recover your capital before the dirt can be taken back.
fields.example: Payback with one tenant runs about 15 years on a $275,000 build at $2,000 a month and a 75 percent margin [Mr. Money — jQ79QHMZWQE @ 00:02:30]. The ground lease has 11 years remaining, the exact live exposure Holly Lane Radio flags under a producing tower [Holly Lane Radio — RRrHddpY1pU @ 00:17:58]. Gap: four years; extension required before any purchase.

fields.name: landowner_buyout_cross_check
fields.prompt: If you own the ground under a tower, list every buyout multiple quoted to you and compare it against the ranges practitioners report. Note how far your renewal date is and whether the approach letter arrived suspiciously friendly and early.
fields.example: Offer received at 12 times rent. Selina Gonzales describes 15 to 20 times as typical, peaking near 21 times in 2024, with anything under 15 the cheap side [Selina Gonzales — x2ZfqDSKoOI @ 00:07:17]. Renewal is five years out, and Gonzales warns never to sell then, because the approach is designed to land soft: the letter is friendly.

fields.name: permit_classification
fields.prompt: Classify the billboard permit as conforming or nonconforming and record your state's position on re-erection after damage. Note whether destruction by weather or by vandalism changes the outcome, and price the board only after this classification is complete.
fields.example: The permit is nonconforming, so the board can be maintained but not rebuilt [Cashflow Anatomy — GzFGSTXAVaI @ 00:06:46]. A grandfathered sign destroyed by vandalism or other criminal or tortious acts may return only where state law permits and only in kind; weather damage does not qualify [Cashflow Anatomy — GzFGSTXAVaI @ 00:02:59]. Storm risk therefore caps my offer.

fields.name: ground_lease_permit_transfer
fields.prompt: Confirm the billboard ground lease length, renewal rights, and rent as a share of revenue, and verify the permit actually transfers to you. Record advertiser contracts on hand and twelve months of real occupancy rather than seller projections.
fields.example: Ground lease shows 14 years remaining plus two renewals, at about 18 percent of gross. Acquisition Insider requires 10-plus years with renewals, a permit that transfers, advertiser contracts, and 12 months of real occupancy [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:05:22]. Seller supplied only nine months of invoices, so three months of occupancy remain unverified and the price is held.

fields.name: static_board_cash_flow
fields.prompt: Build the cash flow for a single static board using price per face, occupancy, operating costs, and ground lease share. Apply a trading multiple to that cash flow and compare the result with the asking price before negotiating with the seller.
fields.example: A two-sided static board at $600 per face per month and 80 percent occupancy, with roughly 40 percent costs including a 15 to 20 percent ground lease, nets about $7,000 a year and trades at 8 to 10 times, or $55,000 to $70,000 [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:02:07]. The seller asks $95,000, well above that band.

fields.name: dot_reroute_and_traffic
fields.prompt: Call the state DOT about planned construction or bypasses near the board and pull the DOT traffic count yourself. Record the contact, date, findings, and any difference between the official count and the figure the seller provided.
fields.example: Boards all over America stare at bypassed asphalt because buyers checked revenue and never asked about reroutes [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:04:30]. Called the district office on March 3: a bypass is in design for 2029. DOT count shows 14,200 daily vehicles versus the seller's 21,000 claim. Both findings go into the offer letter as price adjustments.

fields.name: permit_roll_sourcing
fields.prompt: Pull the state DOT outdoor advertising permit roll for your target corridor and list independent owners by name. Note zoning history for each site, including any rezoning requested specifically to erect a billboard, and the direct-mail approach you will use.
fields.example: The permit roll lists 42 boards held by six mom-and-pop owners, the same channel Lamar uses for tuck-in acquisitions [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:05:06]. Meeting minutes show one parcel was rezoned specifically to get a billboard erected, which INDOT reviewers flag as against the law [INDOT — YWN-XPL47M0 @ 00:11:00]. Exclude it; write the other five directly.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the tower clears two signed tenants or is rejected, anchor loss and carrier default are stress-tested, land control covers payback, the billboard permit is classified and confirmed transferable, DOT traffic and reroute findings are logged, and the offer sits inside the documented cash-flow multiple band.

worksheets.title: Billboard Startup and Unit Economics Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Convert a candidate billboard site or acquisition into a permit-first, occupancy-realistic operating plan, so that land control, landowner terms, conversion decisions, storm exposure, and debt are all decided before steel is ordered or capital is wired.
instructions: Start with the permit field and stop if the permit is unverified or nontransferable; every downstream number depends on the permit, not the structure.
Use the DOT traffic count and construction plans, never figures supplied by the seller, when completing the site filter and exit fields.
Underwrite occupancy at 85 percent or lower and show the breakeven fill explicitly; do not enter any revenue figure based on full rate card.
Write lease language as you would propose it to the landowner, including rent commencement triggers, cancellation rights, removal limits, and recording instructions.
Revisit the leverage field after every change to revenue or rent assumptions, and rerun the 6 percent versus 9 percent interest test each time.

fields.name: permit_status_verification
fields.prompt: Record the exact permit status for the target board or site, including whether the permit is conforming or nonconforming, whether it transfers to you, and the date you confirmed it, before any steel, deposit, or ground lease commitment is made.
fields.example: Permit confirmed transferable before ordering steel, because building first is how beginners end up with 'a very expensive pole' [Global Finance Desk — AkX52_z30r4 @ 00:09:45]. The board is grandfathered under the Highway Beautification Act, so supply stays frozen and the permit, not the structure, is the asset I am paying for [The Finance Explainer — pHu5ZfxNtfg @ 00:06:17].

fields.name: site_traffic_filter
fields.prompt: Enter the daily vehicle count for the proposed billboard location, the source of that count, and whether it falls inside the operator band, then note any planned reroute or bypass that could strand the face on dead asphalt within the lease term.
fields.example: Corridor falls inside the 10,000 to 20,000 daily vehicle band operators filter for, measured with the DOT count, never the seller's [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:04:30]. I called the DOT about construction plans before closing and found no reroute. More eyeballs raise value, so 'think of your billboard as like a mini mall' [Clear Multifamily — LMD9ecO4o1M @ 00:02:51].

fields.name: land_control_structure
fields.prompt: Describe how you will control the dirt under the structure, whether a ground lease, a recorded easement, or owned land, and explain why that choice fits your capital, timeline, and exit, including what happens if the state takes the property.
fields.example: Ground lease, recorded with the county before ordering steel, because an unfiled 50-year lease left one operator with no reimbursement after the state took the property [The Bell Board Podcast — r6MxdTpj3sg @ 00:01:31]. An easement was priced but rejected, since 'Easements usually require a lump sum of 8 to 15 years of rent paid upfront' [Robert_Wallace — 0Lv5_kKNNWg @ 00:03:20].

fields.name: rent_commencement_clause
fields.prompt: Write the exact rent commencement trigger and cancellation language you will propose to the landowner, naming which milestones must occur before the first rent check, and the walk-away right you keep if the permit application is denied or stalls.
fields.example: Rent begins only after permits issue, the structure is finished, and ads are posted, so I never pay monthly land rent from the signing date [Robert_Wallace — hxwD9JLVZs8 @ 00:05:42]. The lease also carries the clause that 'Smart operators add': the right to cancel without penalty if the permits fail [Mr. Money — t4mEx2qxaZ8 @ 00:04:49].

fields.name: landowner_revenue_split
fields.prompt: State the landowner compensation structure you will offer, flat rent, percentage of gross, or the higher of the two, with the exact percentage, escalator cap, and lease term, and explain how it protects both parties over a twenty-year horizon.
fields.example: Opening letter offers a low flat rate or 18-20% of revenue, whichever is higher, which 'protects the landowner from inflation and keeps them happy' [Bama Billboards — rxbKA112Tdc @ 00:02:54]. Escalators are capped at 2-3% on a 20-year term, and expirations are staggered so the portfolio never resets at once [Felix Finance — Zfn3IARm5no @ 00:05:04].

fields.name: occupancy_underwriting
fields.prompt: Underwrite the board's revenue at a realistic fill rate rather than rate card, listing sold weeks per year, the price per block, the breakeven fill, and how far occupancy can fall before the board loses money after fixed costs.
fields.example: Underwritten at 85% occupancy, about 44 sold weeks per year, never full rate card [Walt Runs The Numbers — 9d5MJAQGDk8 @ 00:06:58]. Using the $40,000 build model at $2,000 per four-week block across 13 blocks, breakeven sits near 38% fill and 35% fill loses about $800 [Econometrics — q9ejuh31AvI @ 00:03:20]. Discounting stays one-off, never the norm.

fields.name: digital_conversion_case
fields.prompt: Lay out the case for or against converting this static face to digital, including conversion cost, current monthly static revenue, projected digital revenue at realistic slot fill, and the specific condition that must be proven before capital is committed.
fields.example: Conversion runs about $200,000 and could lift a face from roughly $3,000 a month static to $15,000-$18,000 digital [Rio Explains — OYv2q23Z36g @ 00:03:05]. The inventory goes from two ads to sixteen [Ken McElroy — bteMgQqmSCk @ 00:00:58]. Deferred until the static face proves demand, because three of six slots sold at $1,500 halves gross from $9,000 to $4,500.

fields.name: storm_and_nonconforming_plan
fields.prompt: Document your storm-damage protocol for a nonconforming structure, covering who strips the faces, how repair cost is totaled against replacement value, which records are kept, and what you will do if the structure cannot legally be rebuilt.
fields.example: Before repairing any storm-damaged non-conforming sign, I total the cost against roughly 50% of replacement value and document every repair [Business Breakdown — exXUEqaAB2k @ 00:11:18]. Warning: 'She could not replace it' [Business Breakdown — exXUEqaAB2k @ 00:12:07]. Faces come off at the onset of a storm so the structure better withstands high winds [Plain Sight — Nuf8IbOuL70 @ 00:22:38].

fields.name: ground_lease_red_flags
fields.prompt: List every clause in the existing ground lease that could impair value, including right of first refusal, tear-down obligations, removal duties, renewal terms, and whether the lease is recorded, and price the board only after each is cleared.
fields.example: Read the ground lease for right-of-first-refusal and tear-down clauses before pricing [ledgerandland — 6oamhwKj2wU @ 00:10:33]. Removal duties are limited to above-ground portions only [Robert_Wallace — hxwD9JLVZs8 @ 00:09:27]. The lease runs 10-plus years with renewals and the permit transfers with advertiser contracts and 12 months of real occupancy [Acquisition Insider — 4PyMov-VjoE @ 00:05:22].

fields.name: leverage_and_exit
fields.prompt: Stress-test the debt load and exit value, modeling interest at two rates, renewal rent at double, the exit multiple you expect a buyer to pay, and the minimum cash cushion required so the mortgage never crushes a producing board.
fields.example: Interest is stress-tested at 6% versus 9%, and I refuse to enter undercapitalized at $20K [Money Mechanics — PIQPl5zhm5s @ 00:21:27]. Renewals are modeled at double rent, the scenario that bankrupted a 300-board, 75%-debt roll-up in 2021 [Behind The Billions — Bb-6A1zEJAc @ 00:07:54]. Exit assumes 7-12x revenue, $670,000 to $1M+ on $96,000 a year [Profit Mechanics — chCNj5IEUZw @ 00:22:10].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not order steel, sign a ground lease, or fund an acquisition until the permit is confirmed transferable, the lease is recorded with the county, rent commencement is tied to permits and posted ads, and the board survives 85 percent occupancy at 9 percent interest.

worksheets.title: Ad Sales Engine and IOS Market Screen
worksheets.purpose: Build a repeatable process for selling billboard and alternative faces on location, rate, and occupancy, then apply the same discipline to screening industrial outdoor storage yards where zoning, usable dirt, and tenant demand decide the deal.
instructions: Fill the six ad-sales fields for every face in inventory, not just the strongest boards, so dead inventory surfaces early.
Attach a spec ad and a tracking plan to every proposal before a contract is drafted or sent.
Treat the 75-80 percent occupancy band as the switch point between pushing fill and pushing rate, and record which side each face sits on.
For the IOS fields, obtain zoning confirmation in writing from the municipality and local land use counsel before entering any rent or cap rate assumption.
Measure usable acres on site and against the survey, then price rent and debt only on the usable figure.

fields.name: occupancy_rate_band
fields.prompt: Record current occupancy for each face you sell, the band at which your team stops chasing fill and starts pushing rate, and the contract length mix you will accept, including any premium charged for campaigns shorter than three months.
fields.example: Below 75-80% occupancy the team pushes fill; above that band it pushes rate [The Bell Board Podcast — N6EyLPQ9NhA @ 00:25:03]. Contracts follow the norm that 'The minimum is usually 3 months, 6 or 12 months is typical,' and anything shorter costs a premium [Billboard Source — gReq9TXl5BY @ 00:01:18]. Panels are ranked by revenue per panel, rural to digital corridor.

fields.name: spec_ad_pipeline
fields.prompt: Describe how every prospect and renewal will see a spec ad before any contract appears, who designs it, how quickly it is delivered, and how the creative is kept short enough to read at highway speed and distance.
fields.example: Every prospect and every renewal sees a spec ad first, because reps who arrive with only a contract, map and photos are selling a car nobody has seen [Tasty Ad — ivfNhpDax7I @ 00:00:53]. Creative stays at 7-8 words maximum to suit dwell time and read distance, and sales go direct for the highest margin [The Finance Explainer — pHu5ZfxNtfg @ 00:06:59].

fields.name: dead_inventory_recovery
fields.prompt: Name the faces that have sat empty longest, the incentive you will pay reps to fill them, the vacancy signage on each, and the date by which an unanswered sign triggers a direct-mail campaign to nearby businesses.
fields.example: Any face empty 90 days carries a double-commission bounty [The Bell Board Podcast — N6EyLPQ9NhA @ 00:13:11]. Each vacancy shows a 'Rent this sign' face, white letters on red with a phone number; no call within 30 days triggers 500 flyers at about $1 each, where a 1% response yields five calls [CREUniversity — QDvEU9XEEA4 @ 00:02:14].

fields.name: programmatic_bid_plan
fields.prompt: Set your programmatic bid strategy for any network digital face, stating the default bid, your chosen bid, the expected cost per blip, slot length under state rules, and how certified circulation data supports the rate you quote advertisers.
fields.example: Blips clear around 2-6 cents each on 6-8 second slots [Local Marketing Institute — uoJvU0CyoBY @ 00:49:54]. Bids run at $0.50, above the $0.35 default, because 'our algorithm favors the higher' bid [Local Marketing Institute — uoJvU0CyoBY @ 00:48:29]. The board's daily effective circulation gets Geopath-certified, since a certified 80K DEC commands 40-60% more [The Money Mindset HQ — JCnJw5eFyEE @ 00:01:32].

fields.name: alternative_formats
fields.prompt: Evaluate one alternative face format beyond the fixed roadside board, such as a mobile LED truck or indoor screen network, listing day or monthly rates, advertisers per screen, equipment specifications that matter, and the monthly gross at realistic booking.
fields.example: An LED truck books $1,200-1,800 a day on routes and $2,500-3,600 a day at events, so 10 event days a month grosses $12K-18K [Cant Miss US — o3KgQJFdGXQ @ 00:01:10]. Power matters: 'Most trucks are underpowered at 8, 10 or 12 kW' [Mobile Digital Billboard University | Jerry Teeter — mG9J2Z6RgSY @ 00:02:56]. Indoor screens carry 5-10 advertisers at $100-300 monthly.

fields.name: campaign_tracking_stack
fields.prompt: List the tracking tools attached to each advertiser campaign before launch, explain how response data will be reported back at renewal, and note the day-parting schedule for digital slots that matches each advertiser to the hours their customers drive past.
fields.example: No launch without a dedicated URL or landing page, QR retargeting, call tracking, an SMS short code, and asking callers where they heard of you [Adrian Boysel — 14aRU-ObgC0 @ 00:09:01]. Digital slots are day-parted, coffee in the morning and restaurants in the evening, with 6-10 slots on an 8-second rotation [Hidden Economics — XlZ7pkhH2fM @ 00:02:17].

fields.name: ios_zoning_by_right
fields.prompt: Confirm in writing whether outdoor storage is allowed by right, conditional, or only as a grandfathered nonconforming use on the target yard, naming the land use counsel retained and the municipal officials met about allowed activities and future tenants.
fields.example: Outdoor storage is confirmed by right, not conditional, and not a grandfathered legal non-conforming use that disappears when the tenant leaves [MaxLife Commercial RE MLR — oYtLEutv1NQ @ 00:04:00]. Local land use counsel met the municipality on allowed activities and future tenant types, because the top three challenges are zoning, zoning, and zoning [CREDA Global — cKtqug8KPPk @ 00:01:12].

fields.name: usable_acreage_net
fields.prompt: Measure gross acres against usable acres after landscaping, retention, and setbacks, record building coverage as a share of the site, and confirm a 53-foot trailer can turn in, since tenants may pay only for the ground they can actually use.
fields.example: The 2-acre site measures as 1.5 usable acres net of landscaping, retention and setbacks, and tenants may pay only on usable area [EdisonIndustrial — Wu_IobArlaI @ 00:02:48]. Coverage stays under 25 percent. On the tour, a 53-foot trailer turned in cleanly, the test Justin Horowitz runs on every site [Industrial Real Estate Show — yb3YiKWxoFg @ 00:06:44].

fields.name: ios_pricing_and_debt
fields.prompt: Underwrite the acquisition cap rate against the stabilized trade, months of modeled vacancy, per-acre rent, site-work budget per acre, and the debt yield and coverage ratio your lender requires, flagging any premium for managed truck parking debt.
fields.example: Buying at 8.5% against 7% stabilized trades after modeling 6 to 8 months of vacancy, with Atlanta rent around $5K per acre per month [Industrial Real Estate Show — LftC_mcL69E @ 00:14:54]. Debt sizes to a 10% debt yield and 1.25x DSCR; managed truck parking needs 12-13% [Industrial Real Estate Show — yb3YiKWxoFg @ 00:21:12].

fields.name: environmental_and_demand_check
fields.prompt: Record the environmental diligence completed on the yard, including Phase I findings, insurance bound, holdbacks negotiated, and emerging contaminant flags, then note whether demand for this site size is deep or thin in the submarket you are buying.
fields.example: Phase I ordered, environmental insurance bound from day one, and holdbacks negotiated pending no-further-action letters, with PFAS flagged as an emerging issue [Industrial Real Estate Show — yb3YiKWxoFg @ 00:26:50]. The site is 2 acres, inside the 1 to 3 acre range users want, avoiding the 5 to 7 acre band where Industrial Advisors calls demand overstated.

worksheets.completion_gate: No face is considered sold until a spec ad was shown and tracking is live, and no IOS yard proceeds to contract until outdoor storage is confirmed by right, usable acres are measured, the Phase I is complete, and debt sizes to a 10 percent debt yield and 1.25x DSCR.

worksheets.title: Yard Operations and Under-the-Lease Infrastructure Audit
worksheets.purpose: Turn an approved IOS or truck parking site into a built, gated, paying yard, and audit any cell or battery storage lease on the property for grid, structural, and obsolescence risk before committing land for decades.
instructions: Complete the jurisdiction and easement fields before signing a purchase contract; a friendly city and clean title come before any build budget.
Price every build line from current quotes and compare against the fence, gate, light, and base-material benchmarks operators report.
Model stall income net of insurance, bad debt, vacancy, and late payments, and rerun the model whenever an insurance quote changes.
For battery storage, confirm substation capacity with the utility and slope with contour lines and soil survey, never with the listing.
For cell sites, reconcile on-site equipment against the lease and record any structural analysis before new panels are approved.

fields.name: jurisdiction_friendliness
fields.prompt: Before going under contract, record your conversation with the city about the intended yard use, the officials you spoke with, the certificate-of-occupancy steps they described, and whether the jurisdiction signaled it would actually sign off on the use.
fields.example: The city confirmed friendly before contract, because 'The city is the number one issue' [Ronald Rohde Law — gcg4K6xqYaU @ 00:05:42]; Ron's 5.5-acre site drew 50 to 75+ tours and still could not lease without approval. The certificate-of-occupancy process was mapped first, the step Ron wishes they had mastered early [Tyler Cauble — q7HQGiIiT_8 @ 00:32:22].

fields.name: land_basis_and_easements
fields.prompt: Enter the per-acre land basis for the proposed yard, the number of recorded easements found in title, and any easement that could delay construction or raise cost, confirming the basis still allows the yard to cash flow at realistic stall rents.
fields.example: Basis is viable: 'At $1M per acre the site likely won't cash flow, while $50,000 to $100,000 per acre is viable' [Ronald Rohde Law — rPXHwXgqWs8 @ 00:01:28]. Every easement was pulled before closing; Chris Long lost 2 years and saw costs rise by a third on a site carrying 12 easements [Garret Wong Podcast — RPNJmiZNQdY @ 00:39:23].

fields.name: yard_build_budget
fields.prompt: Itemize the yard build budget, including fencing per linear foot, the gate and operator, light poles, base material choice between gravel and asphalt millings, and explain how you will fund improvements from rent rather than a large upfront reserve.
fields.example: Chain link at $16 per linear foot, light poles at $1,000 each, and a 30 ft cantilever gate at about $30K installed plus a $5K operator [Ronald Rohde Law — rPXHwXgqWs8 @ 00:06:59]. Base is asphalt millings at $30 per truck instead of $800 gravel [Industrial Real Estate Show — LftC_mcL69E @ 00:29:41]. Rents rise at closing to fund the value-add.

fields.name: stall_pricing_and_noi
fields.prompt: Model stall count per acre, monthly rent per stall, expected occupancy, and resulting net operating income after taxes, insurance, management, utilities, and software, and note how insurance increases could offset any rent lift you achieve after stabilization.
fields.example: One acre at about 40 spaces times $175 a month grosses $7,000 a month, roughly $57K NOI with occupancy in the mid-to-upper 90s [Tyler Cauble — q7HQGiIiT_8 @ 00:19:30]. Rohde pushed stalls from $100 to $215-225, yet higher insurance kept net income flat [Ronald Rohde Law — gcg4K6xqYaU @ 00:04:24], so insurance is re-quoted before any rent assumption.

fields.name: access_and_payment_control
fields.prompt: Describe the gate and access system you will run, how access is tied to payment, how inbound calls are answered, and the metric you will track for average revenue per space after bad debt, vacancy, and late payments.
fields.example: Gate access is tied to payment, and average revenue per space is tracked net of bad debt, vacancy and late payments [Truck Parking Media — ulBXkeE5I_8 @ 00:02:13]. Calls are answered live, because callers dial three yards at once and a 20-minute callback lost bookings [Truck Parking Media — ulBXkeE5I_8 @ 00:02:30]. SIM cards at about $10 each replace commercial Wi-Fi.

fields.name: marketplace_or_recapture_play
fields.prompt: If you will monetize spare spaces through a parking marketplace or recapture excess acreage from an underutilized yard, record the revenue split or give-back terms, the expected cap rate change, and the location test that proves demand exists nearby.
fields.example: Truck Parking Club starts hosts at a 70/30 owner/platform split covering marketing, payments and 24/7/365 support [REtipster — Ombo8TjihMk @ 00:12:41]. The recapture play: the tenant gives back 1.5 acres to save $3,000 a month, re-leased at $6,000 NNN to turn a 6.25 cap into an 8 [Jonathan Hayek — mPrS0VognEo @ 00:22:53]. Remote rural land is excluded.

fields.name: bess_site_screen
fields.prompt: Screen the parcel for a battery storage lease by recording acreage, measured distance to the nearest substation, capacity confirmed directly with the utility, slope and soil conditions, and access, then state whether the parcel passes or fails each threshold.
fields.example: Parcel falls inside the 2 to 15 acre range developers want, with the substation less than half a mile away [LandApp by LandGate — Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:33]. Capacity was confirmed with the utility, because 'The listing tells you what you want to hear' [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:53]. Contour lines and soil survey were checked for 6 to 10% slopes.

fields.name: bess_lease_terms
fields.prompt: Draft the battery storage lease terms you will require, including total term length, facility upgrade rights, the state incentives you researched before negotiating, and the point in the project timeline at which you are willing to commit the land.
fields.example: Term runs 20 to 30 years and must allow periodic facility upgrades as technology changes [LandApp by LandGate — Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:01:44]. State renewable energy incentives were studied first, since few owners know them [LandApp by LandGate — Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:51]. Timing is the price: too early carries planning, land and grid risk [Gore Street Capital — 9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:05:40].

fields.name: tower_equipment_and_structure
fields.prompt: For any cell site on your property, record the sectors and antennas present, whether a structural analysis preceded heavier 5G panels, and which carriers occupy the structure, noting any equipment installed outside the lease lines that creates a renegotiation opening.
fields.example: Three sectors, each with antennas covering 120 degrees [Telecom Training — tqz39K230_w @ 00:01:27]. A structural analysis ran before the heavier 5G panels, since sometimes the answer is reinforce the pole first [Buildrightacademy — kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:15:43]. Equipment was reconciled against the lease, because space used outside the lease lines hands the owner a renegotiation opening [Vertical Consultants — F1m9euwLJAQ @ 00:12:42].

fields.name: obsolescence_and_battery_risk
fields.prompt: Assess the long-term obsolescence risk to the lease income on your site, covering satellite or microcell substitution for tower rent and annual battery degradation with reserve sizing for storage, and state the assumption you will hold in your model.
fields.example: SpaceX's reported push for at least 80,000 cell sites is noted [The Space Flight — 0P3b6pUkElk @ 00:06:48], but the model holds that 'Satellite is a supplement, not a substitute' [Vertical Consultants — BoWyq83WIVk @ 00:00:21]. Storage cash flow assumes 1.5 to 3.5% annual battery fade and a 20% reserve, with cooling holding cells between 20 and 40 degrees C.

worksheets.completion_gate: No yard opens until the city has signed off, the certificate of occupancy is issued, every easement is cleared, and gate access is tied to payment; no battery or cell lease is signed until utility capacity, upgrade rights, structural analysis, and a written obsolescence assumption are on file.
